coverage_note: Municipal employees under the Vermont Municipal Employee Relations Act, 21 V.S.A. chapter 22. State employees (State Employees Labor Relations Act, 3 V.S.A. chapter 27), teachers and school administrators (16 V.S.A. chapter 57) and other groups have separate statutes not covered by this row.

governing_statute.quote: This chapter shall be known as the Vermont Municipal Employee Relations Act.

labor_board.value: Vermont State Labor Relations Board (3 V.S.A. 921); impasse mediation and fact-finding run through the Commissioner of Labor
labor_board.quote: “Board” means the State Labor Relations Board established under 3 V.S.A. § 921.

ulp_limitation_period.value: Six months from the unfair labor practice to the filing of the charge with the Board, extended for armed-forces service; the Board may waive the period if the aggrieved person did not understand that an unfair labor practice had occurred or the offending person actively concealed it
ulp_limitation_period.quote: No complaint shall issue based on any unfair labor practice occurring more than six months prior to the filing of the charge with the Board unless the person aggrieved thereby was prevented from filing the charge by reason of service in the U.S. Armed Forces, in which event the six-month period shall be computed from the day of his or her discharge. The Board may waive the six-month period if it finds that: (1) the aggrieved person did not understand that an unfair labor practice had been perpetrated against him or her; or (2) the offending person had actively concealed his, her, or its perpetration of that unfair labor practice.

who_may_bargain.value: Employees of cities, towns, villages and other municipal employers, including municipal school employees, excluding elected officials and board members, executive officers, supervisors, probationary and confidential employees, and (except as section 1735 provides) certified school employees
who_may_bargain.quote: “Municipal employee” means any employee of a municipal employer, including a municipal school employee or a professional employee as defined in subdivision 1502(11) of this title, except: (A) elected officials, board and commission members, and executive officers; (B) individuals employed as supervisors as defined by section 1502 of this title;

source.title: 21 V.S.A. chapter 22, Municipal Employee Relations Act

scope_of_bargaining.value: Wages, hours and conditions of employment, excluding managerial prerogative; for municipal school employees, health care benefits (other than stand-alone vision and dental) are excluded and handled statewide
scope_of_bargaining.quote: shall bargain in good faith with respect to wages, hours, and conditions of employment and shall execute a written contract incorporating any agreement reached; provided, however, that neither party shall be compelled to agree to a proposal nor to make a concession, nor to bargain over any issue of managerial prerogative.

impasse_procedure.value: Mediation by or through the Commissioner of Labor, then fact-finding; binding arbitration only by voluntary agreement or local referendum, except a required arbitration path for municipal public safety employees
impasse_procedure.quote: If the parties are at an impasse in negotiations, either party may petition the Commissioner of Labor to appoint a mediator.

supporting.quote: If after a reasonable period of time not less than 15 days after the appointment of a mediator the impasse is not resolved, the mediator shall certify to the Commissioner of Labor that the impasse continues. The Commissioner shall appoint a qualified fact finder within 30 days of a request by either party.

source.title: 21 V.S.A. chapter 22, Municipal Employee Relations Act

strike_legality.value: Permitted with limits: a strike may be prohibited only if it comes within 30 days after the fact-finder's report, after voluntary submission to binding arbitration or an award, or if it endangers public health, safety or welfare; strikers may not be permanently replaced
strike_legality.quote: (a) A strike shall not be prohibited unless: (1) it occurs sooner than 30 days after the delivery of a factfinder’s report to the parties pursuant to subsection 1732(e) of this title; (2) it occurs after both parties have voluntarily submitted a dispute to final and binding arbitration, or after a decision or award has been issued by the arbitrator; or (3) it will endanger the health, safety, or welfare of the public.

agency_fee_status.value: The statute still authorizes agreed agency service fees (capped at 85 percent of dues), but they cannot be collected from nonconsenting public employees after Janus v. AFSCME (2018)
agency_fee_status.quote: For these reasons, States and public-sector unions may no longer extract agency fees from nonconsenting employees.
